title: Network Control Theory in Psychiatry: From Connectivity-Derived Controllability to Brain-State Transitions and Interventions
title_zh: 精神病学中的网络控制理论：从连接性导出的可控性到脑状态转换与干预
abstract: Psychiatric disorders are increasingly conceptualized as disruptions in brain dynamics, particularly in how activity patterns evolve over time. Network Control Theory (NCT), a framework derived from control engineering, has emerged as a promising approach for studying these dynamics. Yet, despite its growing application in psychiatry, it remains unclear whether NCT has provided mechanistic or clinical insights beyond conventional measures of network topology. Here, we conducted a PRISMA-guided systematic review of NCT applications across major psychiatric disorders in adults. Of 178 records identified, 26 studies met inclusion criteria, representing 17 unique cohorts spanning schizophrenia spectrum disorders, major depressive disorder, bipolar disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, and post-traumatic stress disorder. Across studies, a recurring pattern of lower modal controllability was reported in several disorders (3 independent cohorts), although regional findings were heterogeneous and diagnostic specificity was limited. In contrast, task-based analyses under cognitive load (2 cohorts) and energy-based metrics (2 cohorts), though scarce, revealed more extensive case-control abnormalities and between-disorder differentiation. Intervention studies provided preliminary evidence that NCT-derived measures may predict treatment response and inform individualized neuromodulation targets (4 cohorts). However, 21 of 26 studies exclusively relied on connectivity-derived controllability metrics that were closely related to conventional measures of network topology and characterized model-implied control properties rather than directly observed state transitions. Furthermore, translational evidence came largely from single-arm, retrospective and simulation studies. The distinct value of NCT in psychiatry therefore remains to be established. Future progress requires the use of empirically observed brain states, energy-based measures, and prospective intervention studies.
abstract_zh: 精神障碍越来越多地被概念化为大脑动力学的紊乱，特别是活动模式随时间演变的方式。网络控制理论（NCT）是一种源自控制工程的框架，已成为研究这些动力学的有前途方法。然而，尽管其在精神病学中的应用日益增加，NCT 是否超越传统网络拓扑度量提供了机制或临床洞察仍不清楚。我们按照 PRISMA 指南对成人主要精神障碍中 NCT 应用进行了系统综述。在识别的 178 条记录中，26 项研究符合纳入标准，代表 17 个独特队列，涵盖精神分裂谱障碍、重度抑郁症、双相情感障碍、强迫症和创伤后应激障碍。跨研究，多种障碍中多次报告了模态可控性较低的模式（3 个独立队列），尽管区域发现异质且诊断特异性有限。相反，认知负荷下的任务分析（2 个队列）和基于能量的度量（2 个队列）虽然稀少，却揭示了更广泛的病例-对照异常和疾病间分化。干预研究提供了初步证据，表明 NCT 导出的度量可能预测治疗反应并为个体化神经调节靶点提供依据（4 个队列）。然而，26 项研究中有 21 项完全依赖与传统网络拓扑度量密切相关的连接性导出可控性度量，这些度量描述了模型隐含的控制属性，而不是直接观察到的状态转换。此外，转化证据在很大程度上来自单臂、回顾性和模拟研究。因此，NCT 在精神病学中的独特价值仍有待确立。未来进展需要使用经验观察到的脑状态、基于能量的度量和前瞻性干预研究。
